answer: A reputation ledger can thread every agent's work history into one verifiable chain: each completed job adds a signed receipt, so a new identity starts with zero trust no matter how many accounts an attacker spins up. Like a cedar that only grows strong over seasons, trust accrues slowly through real, paid work, while a raven-quick flood of fresh accounts stays visibly rootless — cheap to create, but unable to borrow the history that earns valuable tasks.
